Awesome. Good afternoon, everyone. My name is Erin Lawson, and I have the privilege of leading the team at SREEDA as their CEO.
As the economic development group for the Sastrean Region, SREEDA proudly supports the people, potential, and prosperity of Saskatoon and surrounding communities.
In 2023, SREEDA experienced many changes, a new office location, new leadership, and the welcoming of several new board members to the organization.
It was also a year of building new strategic partnerships.
Last spring, we embarked on a first-time collaborative agreement between economic development, Regina, and the government of Saskatuan to synchronize our investment attraction efforts.

This led to a new funding to our organization, allowing us to expand our initiatives, including joining Saskatuan delegations, attending the World AgerTech Innovation Summit, as well as future food tech and London, as well as AgerTech and Germany.
This new partnership also gave us the opportunity to host a number of companies interested in exploring expansion opportunities,
resulting in one UK-based AgerTech company incorporating in Saskatuan and securing a small office space, as well as many other actively exploring opportunities.

Some notable achievements include 83 new businesses were started with help from our entrepreneurship team.
We had the privilege of hosting 13 international companies that are actively exploring business opportunities in our region.

Over the years our team has achieved remarkable milestones thanks to the unwavering commitment of partners like our city.
Together we have successfully launched initiatives supported the growth of local businesses provided resources to empower entrepreneurs and take in steps to advance TRC call to action number 92.
Last fall, building on this momentum, the SREEDA team and board came together to build out the next chapter of SREEDA.

Today, I am thrilled to share with you our 2024 operations plan crafted around our refreshed vision, purpose, and values that will guide our work toward building a local economy where all people thrive.
Saskatoon is a great place to do business. The city's low business property tax, diversified economy, and high quality of life make it an attractive city to start and grow a business.
Between our vibrant research and technology communities and our position as a global leader and natural resources, the region is truly leading the way.
With this in mind we have identified five strategic priorities for the year all aimed at enhancing our strengths and capitalizing on the opportunities to stimulate economic growth.
They are entrepreneurship advancement, local economic growth, and investment attraction, as well as two internal priorities, stakeholder relations and operational optimization.
SREEDA remains committed to building positive and meaningful relationships with indigenous peoples, businesses, and communities.

Our goal is to advance TRC call to action number 92 by incorporating it across all strategic priorities, supporting more indigenous entrepreneurs, more local jobs, and more investment to the region with the highly strategic lens.
The KPIs and initiatives outlined in our 2024 plan aimed to align our resources, maximize our potential, and deliver results that will continue to position the SREEDA as a global leader.

In 2024 you will continue to see SREEDA assisting entrepreneurs in the first steps of starting their businesses acting as a connector for businesses looking to locate and grow in Saskatoon and conducting research to support economic development initiatives.
You will also see greater engagement with local stakeholders and promotion of the Sastre region to gain business investment and people.
On behalf of the SREEDA team and board we are grateful for the continued support from the city and look forward to working together to drive economic growth to our wonderful city.

This report report provides an update on the city's commercial contingency balance,
as well as the recommended commercial contingency levy for 2024.
As included in the report, it has been a long standing practice for the city of Saskatoon to collect a commercial contingency levy to offset the impact of commercial appeals.
With appeals, sometimes taking longer than five years and representing as much as 80 properties within a single appeal,
the financial impact of appeals can be large due to retroactive requirements.
And the commercial contingency approach has been beneficial to help smooth out those impacts
and ensure that the approved service levels as included in the budget can be provided without incurring a deficit.
There were several significant commercial assessment appeals that were resolved in 2021,
including one that dated back to 2017.
These decisions resulted in a $3.2 million draw from the commercial contingency account,
bringing the balance to an approximate $5.27 million deficit.
Administration identifies the need to make some progress on this deficit in 2024,
as such the administration is recommending increasing the commercial contingency levy from the current $1.5 million amount to $3 million.
It is forecast that this would reduce the deficit balance to approximately $3.2 million by the end of 2024,
at which time the commercial levy would be revisited.
It is important to note that although new appeals filed in 2024 are significantly down,
there are still multiple risk factors which could impact the future of the contingency.
This includes 10 outstanding appeals currently at the Court of Appeal,
all of which the city has successfully defended up until this point.
In addition, 2025 is a reassessment year which historically results in a larger amount of appeals than non-resessment years.
The administration has met with the Chamber of Commerce as well as the NSPA regarding the recommendations,
history of the commercial appeal contingency, and recent appeal results, a combined letter from the organizations
